documentTypes.name: Standard (Normative)
documentTypes.description: An officially approved document (ANSI/ISA or IEC) containing mandatory normative requirements that systems, components, or programmes must satisfy to ensure industrial automation and control systems (IACS) cybersecurity.
documentTypes.beginnerExplanation: Think of a standard as an official rule or regulation that organisations and manufacturers must comply with to guarantee industrial cybersecurity.

documentTypes.name: Technical Specification (TS)
documentTypes.description: Provides detailed and specific technical guidance in areas where technology is continuously evolving.
documentTypes.beginnerExplanation: A Technical Specification is an advanced technical guide that offers detailed specifications before a full standard is finalised.

documentTypes.name: Technical Report / Technical Specification (TR/TS)
documentTypes.description: Provides informative information, case studies, and best practices.
documentTypes.beginnerExplanation: A Technical Report does not contain strict 'shall' rules, but rather best practices and practical examples to help you understand how to apply standards.

documentTypes.name: Publicly Available Specification (PAS)
documentTypes.description: A rapidly published document to address urgent industry requirements.
documentTypes.beginnerExplanation: A PAS is a provisional solution or fast-tracked specification published because industry needed immediate guidance.

categories.name: General Group
categories.description: Includes documents that address topics common to the entire series.
categories.summary: The General group establishes the theoretical foundations, core concepts, glossary, and fundamental models applicable across the entire 62443 series.

items.title: Concepts and models
items.description: Introduces the terminology, concepts and models used throughout the series.
items.targetAudience: Intended for those unfamiliar with fundamental concepts that form the basis for the series.
items.beginnerExplanation: Explains foundational concepts, terminology, and fundamental models (such as the Purdue reference model and security zones) for beginners.

items.title: Master glossary of terms and definitions
items.description: Terms and abbreviations used throughout the series.
items.targetAudience: All professionals, engineers, and auditors working with ISA/IEC 62443.
items.beginnerExplanation: The official course dictionary containing all approved terms and abbreviations used across all parts of the series.

items.title: System security conformance metrics
items.description: Methodology to develop quantitative metrics derived from the process and technical requirements in the standards.
items.targetAudience: System integrators, security managers, and evaluators.
items.beginnerExplanation: Provides a clear methodology for developing quantitative metrics derived from process and technical requirements.

items.title: IACS security lifecycle and use cases
items.description: Lifecycle for IACS security, as well as several use cases that illustrate various applications.
items.targetAudience: Asset owners, project managers, and security architects.
items.beginnerExplanation: Outlines the IACS security lifecycle and provides practical use cases illustrating real-world industrial applications.

items.title: Scheme for 62443 Cyber Security Profiles
items.description: Specifies a scheme for defining (selecting, writing, drafting, creating) ISA/IEC security profiles.
items.targetAudience: Standards committees, industry groups, and asset owners.
items.beginnerExplanation: Provides the framework and rules for defining and tailoring security profiles suited to specific industrial sectors.

items.title: Application of the 62443 standard in IIoT
items.description: Describes how the ISA/IEC standard can be applied in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) architecture.
items.targetAudience: IIoT architects, device manufacturers, and security engineers.
items.beginnerExplanation: Demonstrates how 62443 standards apply within modern Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) architectures and smart sensors.

categories.name: Policies & Procedures
categories.description: Focuses on the policies and procedures associated with IACS security.
categories.summary: The Policies & Procedures group addresses asset owners, service providers, and administrators responsible for security programmes and patch management.

items.title: Security programme requirements for IACS asset owners
items.description: Describes requirements to define and implement an effective IACS Security Programme.
items.targetAudience: Asset owners responsible for the operation of an IACS security programme.
items.beginnerExplanation: The foundational standard for asset owners explaining how to establish and implement an effective industrial security programme.

items.title: Security protection rating
items.description: Methodology for evaluating the level of protection provided by an operational IACS against the requirements in the ISA/IEC 62443 Series.
items.beginnerExplanation: A rapidly published specification providing a methodology to evaluate the level of protection in an operational IACS.

items.title: Patch management in the IACS environment
items.description: Provides guidance on patch management for IACS.
items.targetAudience: Intended for anyone who has responsibility for the design and implementation of a patch management programme.
items.beginnerExplanation: Essential guidance on applying software patches in industrial environments without compromising safety or production continuity.

items.title: Requirements for IACS service providers
items.description: Requirements for IACS service providers such as system integrators or maintenance providers.
items.targetAudience: System integrators, maintenance providers, and third-party service suppliers.
items.beginnerExplanation: Establishes mandatory requirements that third-party service providers and integrators must meet when servicing industrial systems.

items.title: Implementation guidance for IACS asset owners
items.description: Guidance on what is required to operate an effective IACS Security Programme.
items.targetAudience: Intended for asset owners who have responsibility for the operation of such a programme.
items.beginnerExplanation: Practical advice and detailed guidance for asset owners on operating an effective security programme day-to-day.

categories.name: System Group
categories.description: Addresses requirements at the system level.
categories.summary: The System group focuses on security technologies, system-level risk assessments, and establishing requirements based on Security Levels (SL).

items.title: Security technologies for IACS
items.description: Application of various security technologies to an IACS environment.
items.targetAudience: Intended for anyone who wishes to learn more about the applicability of specific technologies in a control systems environment.
items.beginnerExplanation: Explains how IT security technologies (antivirus, firewalls, encryption) apply within industrial control environments.

items.title: Security risk assessment and system design
items.description: Addresses cybersecurity risk assessment and system design for IACS. Output is Zone & Conduit model and Target Security Levels.
items.targetAudience: Intended for asset owners and system integrators.
items.beginnerExplanation: The primary guide for risk assessment and system design, outputting the Zone & Conduit model and Target Security Levels.

items.title: System security requirements and security levels
items.description: Requirements for an IACS system based on security level.
items.targetAudience: Intended for suppliers of control systems, system integrators, and asset owners.
items.beginnerExplanation: Defines detailed system-level security requirements based on the required Security Level (SL 1 to SL 4).

categories.name: Component Group
categories.description: Provides requirements associated with the development of IACS products.
categories.summary: The Component group addresses product manufacturers and software developers building industrial devices (PLCs, sensors, embedded systems).

items.title: Secure product development lifecycle requirements
items.description: Requirements for a product developer’s security lifecycle.
items.targetAudience: Intended for suppliers of Control System and Component products.
items.beginnerExplanation: Strict requirements regarding the secure development lifecycle for manufacturers building industrial devices and software.

items.title: Technical security requirements for IACS components
items.description: Requirements for IACS Components based on security level (Embedded Devices, Host Devices, Network Devices, Software Applications).
items.targetAudience: Intended for suppliers of Component products that are used in control systems.
items.beginnerExplanation: Technical security requirements for individual components (embedded devices, host components, network devices, and software applications).

categories.name: Profiles Group
categories.description: Planned to contain Profiles for specific domains / areas of interest based on 62443-1-5.
categories.summary: The Profiles group brings together standards dedicated to specific industrial sectors, such as electric energy OT.

items.title: Parts 5-1, 5-2, etc.
items.description: As soon as profiles are published, they will be reflected in the Profiles Group as 62443-5-1, 5-2, etc. ISA99 WG 14 is currently working on Cybersecurity Profiles for Electric Energy OT.
items.targetAudience: Industry sector specialists and asset owners in specific domains.
items.beginnerExplanation: Domain-specific security profiles (e.g. ISA99 WG 14 is currently developing cybersecurity profiles for Electric Energy OT).

categories.name: Evaluation Group
categories.description: Supports evaluators in performing conformity assessments.
categories.summary: The Evaluation group provides methodologies for independent auditors and certification bodies verifying compliance.

items.title: Security evaluation methodology for 62443-2-4
items.description: Security evaluation methodology for evaluating service providers against 62443-2-4.
items.beginnerExplanation: Evaluation methodology to verify whether service providers comply with 62443-2-4 requirements.

items.title: Security evaluation methodology for 62443-2-2 / 4-2
items.description: Security evaluation methodology for components against 62443-4-2 requirements.
items.targetAudience: Independent test labs, component manufacturers, and evaluators.
items.beginnerExplanation: Methodology for testing and evaluating industrial components against 62443-4-2 requirements.
